Rashi on Zevachim 12a:16:1.english: Shall we say Rabbi Yochanan holds, etc.: From the fact that we needed to answer according to him concerning one who designates an offering after midday, it indicates that if one had not heard from him that living animals are permanently disqualified, it would be fitting to designate them forever. For perhaps disqualification applies only to slaughtered animals, as in the case of the scapegoat whose blood is poured out, as discussed in Tractate Yoma (62b).

Rashi on Zevachim 12b:2:1.english: And apostatized from his religion - he is disqualified from bringing an offering, as stated in 'All who slaughter' (Chullin 5b): 'from an ordinary person' excludes an apostate.

Rashi on Zevachim 12b:8:1.hebrew: למה לי למיתני זקן - ליתני זקנים:
Rashi on Zevachim 12b:8:1.english: Why do I need to teach 'zaken' - He should teach 'zekenim'.

Rashi on Zevachim 12b:8:2.hebrew: בחדא - בישיבה אחת היו יושבין וכולן היו כאיש אחד:
Rashi on Zevachim 12b:8:2.english: In one [session] - They were sitting in one session, and all of them were like one man.

Steinsaltz comment #1 on Zevachim 12b:2.english: One who cast off the yoke of Torah and became accustomed to transgression. In another place (see Chullin 5a) it is derived from an inference in the verses (or, in the Rambam's language, 'from oral tradition') that an apostate cannot bring an offering, because 'the sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination' (see Sefer HaMitzvot). And there they distinguish between one who is an apostate to the entire Torah (including an apostate to idolatry or one who publicly desecrates Shabbat) and one who is accustomed to other transgressions: if he became accustomed and was publicly known for a specific transgression, an offering is not accepted from him specifically for that transgression.

Zevachim 12a:16.english: Rabbi Zeira said to Rabbi Abbahu: Shall we say that Rabbi Yoḥanan holds that consecrated animals are disqualified and are no longer fit for sacrifice after they have been disqualified once?
